simple.meaning: בָּמָה (bâmâh) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an elevation.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 104 times across Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, and 12 more, beginning at Leviticus 26:30. Its contexts include sacrifice, altar, city, land, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to בָּמָה (H1116).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: בָּמָה (bâmâh) / H1116 is traced through Leviticus 26:30, Numbers 21:28, Numbers 33:52, Deuteronomy 32:13 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H1116. bamah בָּמָה 104 noun feminine high place (√ apparently בום on account of firm ָ֯ ; compare Assyrian bâmâtê Zim BP 48, Moab. במת MI 3, 27 ) — Jer 48:35 18 t.; הַבָּמָ֫תָה 1Sam 9:13 ; plural בָּמוֺת Num 21:19 62t.; construct בָּֽמֳתֵי Job 9:8 ; Isa 14:14 ; Amos 4:13 ; בָּֽמֳו֯תֵי Deut 32:13 ; Isa 58:14 ; Micah 1:3 (Ew § 211 d Ges § 87 , 5 archaic feminine construct with retracted accent before monosyl. in poetry, bâm©-thê not b©m ); suffix בָּמֹתַי 2Sam 22:34 3 t.; בָּמוֺתַי Psa 18:34 10 t.; — 1 high place, mountain: יָעַר בָּמוֺת forest mountains Micah 3:12 = Jer 26:18 ; עולם במות ancient mountains Ezek 36:2 ; ארנן במות Num 21:28 (E poetry) 2 high places, battle-fields , the chief places of the land giving possession, victory, dominion: במותיך על on thy high places (Gilboa, the battle-field) 2Sam 1:19 , 25 (in 1:19 ᵐ5 has a doublet מֵתֶיךָ thy dead , see We Dr). a. of Israel: ארץ במתי על רכב ride upon the high places of the land Deut 32:13 & Isa 58:14 compare Deut 33:29 ; Psa 18:34 = 2Sam 22:34 ; Hab 3:19 . b. of God: ארץ במתי על דרך tread upon the high places of the earth Amos 4:13 compare Micah 1:3 ; ים במתי Job 9:8 ; עב במתי על עלה (aspiration of the king of Babylon) Isa 14:14 . 3 high places , as places of worship, at first on hills and mountains, later on artificial mounds or platforms, under green trees, and in cities; still later for the chapels erected thereon, and once apparently for a portable sanctuary (decked with diverse colours) Ezek 16:16 . The ancient worship of Israel was conducted on these high places. In the times of Samuel and David they ascended to them, descended from them, and offered sacrifices on them, 1Sam 9:12-25 ; 10:5 , 13 ( הבמה for הביתה We Dr). The custom continued in the reign of Solomon, but Gibeon was הגדולה הבמה 1Kin 3:2-4 compare 1Chr 16:39 ; 21:29 ; 2Chr 1:3 , 13 . High places of Baal were also used Num 22:41 (E) Jer 19:5 ; 32:35 ; of Moab Isa 15:2 ; 16:12 ; Jer 48:35 (compare MI 27 ); these must be demolished Num 33:52 (J). Solomon built במות (platforms or chapels) to Chemosh and Milkom on the Mt. of Evil Counsel opposite Jerusalem 1Kin 11:7 : Jeroboam made temples on the ancient high places of Dan and Bethel 12:31-32 , 2Chr 11:15 ; they are called און במות Hosea 10:8 , ישׂחק במות Amos 7:9 : the kings of Israel built במות and הבמות בתי in all their cities 2Kin 17:9 , and the people worshipped there 17:11 ; these were also used by the mixed population after the exile of Israel 17:29 , 32 (twice in verse): these various idolatrous high places were first destroyed by Josiah 1Kin 13:2 ; 13:32 ; 1 Kings 13:38; 2Kin 23:5-20 2Chr 34:3 . The worship of Yahweh on high places continued in Judah until the exile 1Kin 22:44 ; 2Kin 15:35 ; the sanctity code predicts that Yahweh will destroy them Lev 26:30 ; they were regarded as the reason for the rejection of Shiloh Psa 78:58 . The compiler of Kings, writing from the point of view of the Deuteronomic code, complains סָרוּ לֹא הַבָּמוֺת רַק 2Kin 12:4 ; 14:4 ; 15:4 , 35 compare 2Chr 15:17 ; 20:33 , and praises the few pious kings who destroyed them. a. Rehoboam built במות with מצבות & אשׁרים on every high hill and under every green tree 1Kin 14:23 . b. Asa did not remove the high places 1Kin 15:14 ( 2Chr 14:2 ; 14:4 is incorrect unless בעל במות ). c. Jehoshaphat in his reform on the basis of the covenant code did not remove them 1Kin 22:44 ( אֶתהַֿבָּמוֺת הֵסִיר עוֺד 2Chr 17:16 is doubtless incorrect, possibly read מצבות ); Jehoram, his son, made high places in the cities of Judah 21:11 ( ᵑ9 ᵐ5 ; not mountains HCT); and Ahaz sacrificed on high places on the hills and under every green tree and in every city of Judah 2Kin 16:4 ; 2Chr 28:4 , 25 ; compare Micah 1:5 (read חטאת ? so ᵑ7 ᵑ6 ᵐ5 Che and others; yet compare JBL 1890, 73 f. ) d. Hezekiah removed them 2Kin 18:4 , 22 ; 2Chr 31:1 ; 32:12 ; Isa 36:7 ; but Manasseh rebuilt them 2Kin 21:3 ; 2Chr 33:3 , 19 , and the people continued to sacrifice thereon to Yahweh 33:17 . e. Josiah, in his reform , based on the Deuteronomic code, defiled them and brake them down from Geba to Beersheba 2Kin 23:5 , 8 , 9 ; but subsequently there were התפת במות in the valley of Ben Hinnom Jer 7:31 , and במות throughout Judah 17:3 compare Ezek 6:3 , 6 ; 20:29 (questioned by Ew & Co). 4 funereal mound (?) Ezek 43:7 (Thes, but in their high places AV RV; in their death ᵑ7 Theod Ew Hi RVm), Isa 53:9 (Lowth Ew Bö Rodwell Orelli; but in his death AV RV, or martyr death De Che Br).

He said to me, “Son of man, this is the place of my throne, and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will dwell among the children of Israel forever. The house of Israel will no more defile my holy name, neither they, nor their kings, by their prostitution, and by the dead bodies of their kings in their high places;
The high places also of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed.
For, behold, he who forms the mountains,
The high places of Isaac will be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
